skill.name: github-pr-issue
skill.description: Inspect GitHub pull requests and issues, fetch PR details with comments or diffs, and create or edit GitHub issues and pull requests.
skill.summary: GitHub workflow helper for PR review, issue creation, and pull request updates.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in SKILL.md are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and code fences. The helper script legitimately invokes GitHub CLI authentication and contacts the GitHub API; no obfuscation, prompt injection, or third-party exfiltration was found. The remaining concerns are sensitive token handling and documented workflows that can modify GitHub state.

remediation.suggestion: Document that scripts/read_pr.py reads the GitHub CLI token and contacts api.github.com. Recommend least-privilege token scopes and never log the token.
Require explicit user approval before gh issue create, gh pr new, gh pr edit, or git push. Show the target repository and proposed text first.
Mark mutating command examples as approval-required and keep read-only inspection commands separate from write workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive GitHub Token Handling
semantic_findings.description: scripts/read_pr.py obtains the local GitHub CLI token and uses it as a Bearer token for GitHub API requests. No evidence found that the token is sent outside GitHub, but community code handling credentials requires explicit disclosure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token retrieval and Authorization header construction are explicit, and the API client targets api.github.com. The evidence supports sensitive credential use but not credential exfiltration.

semantic_findings.title: Remote GitHub Write Operations
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs agents to create issues, create pull requests, push branches, and edit PR metadata through GitHub CLI workflows. These are intended capabilities, but they can change remote repository state if run without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow directly names issue creation, PR creation, git push, and PR edit actions. The risk is contextual misuse of legitimate write operations, not hidden code.

content.value_statement: GitHub review and release work can require several commands and repeated context gathering. This skill collects PR context and guides issue or PR changes with structured workflows.
actual_capabilities: View GitHub issues through GitHub CLI guidance.
Fetch PR metadata, comments, reviews, files, commits, stats, bodies, and diffs through read_pr.py.
Format concise pull request titles and descriptions using team-oriented sections.
Create GitHub issues and pull requests with body files instead of interactive editors.
Edit existing issue or PR titles and descriptions after reading current content.
Report GitHub API rate limit details when requested.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication and network access to GitHub.
The helper script only supports github.com pull request URLs.
Can modify remote GitHub resources when write commands are approved.
Does not replace repository-specific review, compliance, or release policies.

use_cases.title: Review Incoming Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Gather a PR summary, changed files, comments, reviews, and diff context before preparing review feedback.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Create a clear PR title and body with summary, key changes, tradeoffs, testing, and notes.

use_cases.title: Create Structured Issues
use_cases.description: Open GitHub issues with concise titles and body text without entering an interactive editor.

prompt_templates.title: View a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to summarize <PR URL>. Include the title, body, changed files, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue for this bug. Use a concise title and a clear body with impact and reproduction details.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pull request for the current branch. Include summary, key changes, constraints, testing, and reviewer notes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze PR Discussion
prompt_templates.prompt: Read <PR URL> with reviews, review comments, issue comments, changed files, stats, and diff. Identify unresolved risks and next actions.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request with comments and changed files.
output: A short PR summary focused on user-visible impact.
A list of main changed areas and review concerns.
A testing summary and suggested follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Create a pull request for the current branch.
output_examples.output: A concise PR title, a structured description, and the final GitHub PR URL after approval.

output_examples.input: Update an existing issue title and body.
output_examples.output: The current issue content is reviewed first, then proposed replacement text is shown before an approved update.

best_practices: Confirm the target repository, branch, and PR or issue URL before running write commands.
Request only the PR sections needed to reduce token use and API calls.
Read existing issue or PR content before replacing titles or descriptions.
anti_patterns: Do not run mutating GitHub commands without explicit user approval.
Do not paste access tokens into prompts, issue bodies, or pull request descriptions.
Do not use the helper script for non-github.com URLs or unrelated repository hosts.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on GitHub CLI commands and authenticated GitHub CLI access.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide noninteractive PR creation after the branch is ready and the user approves the command.

faq.question: Can it read comments and diffs?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script can fetch PR bodies, comments, reviews, files, commits, stats, and diffs.

faq.question: Does it send data outside GitHub?
faq.answer: The reviewed helper targets api.github.com. No evidence found of third-party network destinations in the cited files.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub Enterprise?
faq.answer: No. The helper script validates github.com URLs and does not support other GitHub hosts.

faq.question: Can it edit existing issues or PRs?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires reading the current title or body before editing those fields.
